determinism: the clock is fixed, the root is fixed and the requests are canonical JSON, so every Job, attempt, capability and Artifact identity repeats; patch.sh stands in for /usr/bin/patch with fixed bytes, so the plans and capabilities name the same executable on every host
durable: attempts/ is the workspace-patch-attempts store, capabilities/ the capability store's checkpoint and ledger, tree.json the copy's regular files with their digests, adoption.json what a restarted isolation manager adopts after the apply, after the revert and at the end, parked-record.json the durable record of the Job whose receipt was lost after its child ran
frames: job.submit and job.run of the Runtime-owned copy, then job.plan, job.submit, job.run, job.reconcile and job.result of every workspace.apply-patch@1 and workspace.revert-patch@1 Job, in the order the control plane answered them
inputs: artifacts/job-input-patch/ holds the three unified diffs the recording published before its first request, bound to the host target the patch Jobs name
replayedBy: the Rust port of workspace.apply-patch@1 and workspace.revert-patch@1 (TASK-XPA-015, M3)
source: the production RuntimeControlPlaneHandler over a RuntimeJobEngine whose only provider is WorkspaceOperationsProvider, with EvolutionWorkspaceManager as its isolation manager and WorkspacePatchAttemptStore as its patch lineage, over a fabricated source tree under /private/tmp/arkdeck-workspace-patch-oracle; the patch dispatch loses its receipt only where the sequence says so
why: the job.* corpora carry no frame of these operations and are deduplicated by shape, so they cannot be replayed as one sequence
